text.content: Then Eddie arrived out of the darkness. Eddie is from George. He said something like “finally I’ve caught up with you”. And he basically just said - get up, let’s go and finish this thing.

text.content: Eddie is a pretty big deal in the George trail running scene. He’s started something called the Six Peaks challenge (think 13 peaks but in George). He’s run many milers (his slowest time is 30 hours). He was flown out here by a wealthy mother/son combo who wanted someone to guide them through it. The son had the best name on Earth: Hercules Mugglestone. Sadly they both dropped out around Graskop (about 100km in). And then Eddie started basically sprinting to beat the cutoffs. Eddie had arrived at a few aid stations just as I was leaving them, and I think that he was one of the few people that he hadn’t overtaken. So I suspect that he was kind of chasing me.

text.content: We chatted about all things, some nonsensical conversations. We were coming closer and closer to this aid station called Ceylon, which never seemed to arrive. We had this hilarious shared hallucination whereby the lights of the town of Sabie sometimes appeared between the trees in the darkness of night. They looked like an enormous three story hotel just around the next corner. Eventually I asked if he too had seen the hotel - and he said he was so relieved that I saw it too. As he thought he was going crazy. After about an hour and no hotel we conceded that we had both gone a little crazy. But there was something very comforting of being crazy in company.

But somehow I just trusted whatever subconscious part of my brain was controlling my feet and watched the pretty colours pass by.

text.content: We come flying down a single track at honestly a sub 4 minute/km pace - we can see the lights of Merry Pebbles and the finish line in distance. And then FOK IT screams Eddie from ahead of me. And we come to a stop before a raging river with a single slack line strung across. Eddie goes through his whole vocabulary of both English and Afrikaans swear words then starts walking back muttering to himself. I catch up, we check Google Maps and find that it’s going to be another 5km to avoid the river. So we wade our way through. It was treacherous and freezing. Both a horrible and classic way to end this.
